summary.headline: Berger Paints Q1 FY27 standalone value growth 12.7% on ~8.4% volume; operating margin 17.4%, PAT up 25.5%.
summary.overview: Standalone revenue grew 12.7% in value with volume up about 8.4%, driven by decorative (value +13.5%, operating profit up nearly 20%). Gross margin was 39.3%, held back by delayed and partial price pass-through in industrial and protective, GI and powder coatings, where price increases landed late in the quarter. Consolidated revenue rose 12%, PBDIT rose 12.6%-15% (management cited 15% operating profit growth) with margin up about 40 bps, and PAT rose 28.6%, with the Bolex and STP subsidiaries lagging on growth. Management guided to double-digit FY27 revenue growth, a slightly better Q2 than Q1 on a year-on-year basis, and operating margin within the 15-17% range.

financial_highlights.change: Above 15-17% guided range; Q1 seasonally higher on value sales
Consolidated operating margin just short of 17%

financial_highlights.value: Rs 1,424 crore as of end June 2026
financial_highlights.change: Up from Rs 992 crore (transcript reads 992 to 11.98 to 1424, likely a transcription error)

segments.name: Decorative
segments.commentary: Value growth about 13.5%, the highest in 12 quarters, with operating profit up nearly 20% and margin expansion. Exterior emulsions outperformed; Color Plus premium interior emulsion gaining traction; Luxol metallics new range doing well.

segments.name: Protective, GI and powder coatings
segments.commentary: Relatively lower growth because price increases were taken late in the quarter after a prolonged battle in the field; expected to show up more in Q2.

segments.name: Wood coatings and HomeShield
segments.commentary: Strong growth; wood coatings reported strong double-digit volume growth.

segments.name: Construction chemicals and waterproofing
segments.commentary: Robust volume and value growth; now about 10-12% of the paint business and growing well above paint. Roof pool and seal gaining momentum.

segments.name: Subsidiaries and JVs
segments.commentary: Bolex had flattest revenue on seasonality and UK remained subdued, though Bolex profitability improved. STP profitability improved on mix and price. BNPA and Becker JVs posted strong revenue and profit growth.

guidance_outlook: FY27 double-digit revenue growth expected to sustain, supported by full-quarter price increase impact in Q2 and festive demand.
Q2 revenue growth expected slightly ahead of Q1; Q2 volume growth around 7.5-8%, slightly below Q1's 8.5%.
Price increase contribution expected at about 7.5-8.5% in Q2 versus about 5% in Q1.
Operating margin to stay within the 15-17% guided range; Q2 year-on-year operating margin expected to improve, and Q2 should be slightly better than Q1 on that basis, though not sequentially.
Management expects good top-line and operating profit growth in Q3, with no firm margin call beyond that because of raw material volatility.
Capex for FY27 roughly Rs 600-800 crore; Panagar plant to start at end of this fiscal, plus a plant in Odisha near Jharsuguda.
capex_capacity: FY27 capex roughly Rs 600-800 crore, per management.
Panagar factory to start at end of FY27; second plant in Odisha near Jharsuguda, both funded partly from the cash surplus.
Tinting machine installations crossed 2,100 in the quarter; annual target about 10,000, mostly in under-indexed markets.
Store count above 1,900, with urban stores around 900+ and growing.
Backward integration: emulsions and most resins now made in-house; thickeners being produced in-house; a Dow-linked monomer to be made at Sandhila, Lucknow.
demand_pricing: Volume growth about 8.4%, value growth 12.7%, with price contribution about 5% in Q1 (mostly time-weighted) and mix improvement of roughly 2-3%, per management, which differs from management's normal 0.4-0.5% mix change.
Secondary sales were better than last year because rains were lighter; July growth described as reasonable, and August expected to be similar.
Dealers stocked up ahead of price increases; management expects this to be absorbed by stronger sell-out, with little Q2 destocking risk.
Competition intense: challenger brands aligned dealer price lists within about 5%, raised rebates to large dealers, and continue 10% free-material offers in most packs outside the economy segment.
East India muted; West Bengal government transition expected to take 3-4 months before government contracts restart. Northeast hit by floods in Assam. South and North grew faster.
Retail is the bulk of growth; project business 1-2% faster than retail.

qa_highlights.question: How much of Q1 value growth came from price and mix, and what price increase is expected in Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 price impact about 5% (time-weighted, mostly industrial). Q2 price impact expected around 7.5-8.5%, depending on mix. Management said mix improved in Q1 and should improve further in Q2.

qa_highlights.question: Will Q2 margins expand year-on-year, and what about the full year?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects Q2 operating profit growth to be decent and year-on-year margin to improve, helped by industrial price pass-through and operating leverage. Beyond that, margins depend on raw material prices, so no firm full-year call.

qa_highlights.question: Why is decorative growth below the industry leader's?
qa_highlights.answer: Base effect: the leader degrew last year while Berger grew. Management cited a 3.6% value growth differential and an 8.6% profit differential in the base.

qa_highlights.question: Is volume growth at risk from price increases?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects to maintain high single-digit volume growth through network expansion, the branding campaign, new products and the price increase being absorbed, and sees no volume downside risk.

qa_highlights.question: Will there be post-Diwali price cuts?
qa_highlights.answer: Too early to say; it depends on crude and raw materials. If prices fall substantially, some price reduction in H2 is possible to avoid a price war.

qa_highlights.question: Is there any demand or pricing reason for the weak Bolex and STP subsidiary growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Bolex was seasonally weak in Q1; STP was disrupted by the Jamshedpur plant but has normalised. Corrective measures on less profitable lines in Bolex and STP are expected to lift profitability.

risks_watch: Raw material volatility (crude oil, geopolitics): a sharp fall could widen margins, but could also trigger price cuts and discounting in H2.
Industrial and protective price pass-through still lagging; full effect expected in Q2 and August.
Competitive intensity remains elevated; challenger brands' rebates and free-material schemes could persist.
Mix shift toward low-value, high-volume construction chemicals could keep value growth below volume growth.
Eastern India and Northeast demand; West Bengal transition period.
Subsidiaries: UK operations subdued; Bolex and STP growth flat in Q1 with profitability turnaround still to be proven.
Monsoon and the timing of Diwali for festive-season sell-out.
summary.management_tone: Confident on decorative momentum and the Q2 outlook, but noticeably cautious and hedged on raw material-driven margins, with repeated reference to volatility. Evasive on precise mix and price split and on market share figures.
key_quotes: Value growth, as you have seen already, is at 12.7%.
Operating margins are expected to remain within the guided range, which we have always said, that is between 15% and 17%.
The volume growth will be somewhere around similar levels as, quarter one, slightly below, maybe, you know, so we were at 8.5%, maybe it will be 7.5% to 8%, approximately.

adds.what: Second plant in Odisha near Jharsuguda
Monomer plant at Sandhila, Lucknow (Dow-linked backward integration)

growth.why: Management guides double-digit FY27 revenue growth (midpoint 10% taken as floor), backed by price increases (~7.5-8.5% contribution in Q2 vs ~5% in Q1), festive demand and Q2 volume of 7.5-8%, plus Panagar and Odisha plants with FY27 capex of Rs 600-800 crore; capacity timing is end-FY27 so it adds little within the year.
